Definition: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H3137); Achim, an Israelite:--Achim.
BiblicalUsage: Achim appears once, in Matthew's genealogy: 'Sadoc begat Achim; and Achim begat Eliud,' standing between two names we know no more about than him. Beyond this verse the Bible tells no more of him.
TheologicalSignificance: The genealogy is full of men like Achim — no story, only a place in the chain. I hold that as the point: God's promise did not depend on any one man's fame.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
